newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher, cash remains firm.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher, cash remains firm.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly higher Thursday following a marginal uptick on ACCESS and early talk of steady to firmer cash prices, industry sources said.
July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.18 to $2.19 after settling to the upside Wednesday at $2.171 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, July last traded 0.9 cent higher at $2.18, recovering from a session low of $2.151.
Cash prices at Henry Hub were talked at $2.22-2.24, up slightly from Wednesday's trading range of $2.20-2.23.
Technically, traders still pegged July resistance at $2.21, $2.25 and $2.37. Support remained at $2.055 and $2.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 94 bcf and were now 227 bcf, or 20 percent above year-ago levels. Eastern storage gained 63 bcf and remained 101 bcf, or 17 percent, above last year. Consuming region west inventories, which climbed by 12 bcf last week, continued to lag 1996 levels by 10 percent.

In Wednesday's cash, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas firmed by two to three cents to about $2.20. Midcon pipes were talked up slightly around $2.05. New York city gate gas was quoted about two cents higher in the mid-$2.40s.
